prompt.context: Your client, Middle East Textile, exclusively manufactures and sells Abayas in the local Bahrain market. An Abaya is a full-body garment worn by women in the Middle East. The CEO has just called you and wants to know whether he should buy a new machine for $1 million that will effectively double his capacity of Abaya production. He has asked you to provide an answer within the next half-hour.
prompt.question: How will you advise the CEO on whether to purchase the new $1 million machine?

clarifying_info.a: The company exclusively manufactures and sells Abayas in the local Bahrain market.
An Abaya is a full-body garment worn by women in the Middle East.

clarifying_info.q: What is the company's preferred payback period?
clarifying_info.a: The company typically wants its initial cost back in 5 years.

clarifying_info.q: Is there a company discount rate?
clarifying_info.a: You can ignore the discount rate for this case.
The client exclusively makes Abayas for women in the age group of 19–50 years.
The client has 3 competitors in the market, each with 25% market share (the client holds the remaining 25%). All competitors are operating at maximum capacity currently.

clarifying_info.q: What is the market demand trend?
clarifying_info.a: Market demand is stable and women buy an average of 2 Abayas per year in the target age group (19–50 years).

exhibits.title: Bahrain Population Calculations
exhibits.shows: A table showing the breakdown of Bahrain's population used for market sizing, including total population, domestic vs. expat split, gender split, and age group distributions (0–18 yrs = 45%, 19–50 yrs = 40%, 50+ yrs = 15%)
exhibits.data: Total population: 1 million; Domestic population: 20%; Expats: 80%; Age 0–18: 45%; Age 19–50: 40%; Age 50+: 15%

framework: Profitability of the machine purchase: Will the incremental contribution cover the $1M cost within the 5-year payback window?
Revenue drivers: Volume (units sold) and price per unit
Volume: current market size, client's market share, and any growth in target demographic
Costs: variable cost per Abaya, any additional fixed costs from the machine
Market/external factors: competitor capacity constraints, demand trends, and macro market trends
Expansion possibilities: new age groups, new designs, export markets

questions.prompt: Estimate the number of Abayas currently sold by Middle East Textile in the Bahrain market.
questions.guidance: Candidate should lay out the formula verbally before calculating: Bahrain population × % wearing Abayas × % in target demographic × # bought per year × client market share. Key insight is to distinguish domestic residents from expats (80% are expats who do not wear traditional garb). Strong candidates will ask about expat vs. domestic split and age distribution before calculating.

math.setup: Total market = Bahrain population × (% domestic × % women) × % in target age group × abayas/year. Client sales = total market × market share.
math.answer: Middle East Textile sells approximately 20,000 Abayas per year.

questions.prompt: Should the client buy the $1 million machine? Perform a break-even analysis.
questions.guidance: Candidate should recognize: (1) all competitors are at max capacity so the client can capture 100% of incremental market growth; (2) the domestic target demographic grows over time as younger women (0–18) age into the 19–50 bracket and older women (50+) age out, creating a net increase each year; (3) the relevant metric is incremental contribution margin vs. machine cost over 5 years. Strong candidates will also note the competitor expansion risk.

math.setup: Net annual increase in target-age women = inflow from 0–18 cohort − outflow from 50+ cohort. Incremental Abaya sales = net increase × 2. Incremental contribution = incremental sales × (price − variable cost). Accumulate over 5 years and compare to $1M machine cost.
steps: Annual inflow into 19–50 age group (from 0–18): (45% / 18) × 100,000 = 2,500 women/year
Annual outflow from 19–50 age group (into 50+): (40% / 32) × 100,000 = 1,250 women/year
Net annual increase in target age group: 2,500 − 1,250 = 1,250 women/year
Incremental Abayas sold per year: 1,250 × 2 = 2,500 Abayas
Break-even point: approximately 3.5 years (well within the 5-year payback criterion)
math.answer: Cumulative 5-year contribution of $1,875K exceeds the $1M machine cost by $875K; break-even occurs at approximately 3.5 years.

brainstorming.prompt: The client will only use about 62.5% of the extra capacity from the machine even after 5 years. What other options does the client have to utilize the remaining capacity and grow revenue?

categories.name: Domestic market expansion
ideas: Expand target age group to include younger (under 19) or older (over 50) women
Offer new designs or premium lines to increase purchase frequency
Reduce price to capture market share from competitors

categories.name: Export markets
ideas: Export Abayas to other GCC countries (Saudi Arabia, UAE, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar)
Target diaspora communities in Western markets
Partner with regional retailers or e-commerce platforms

categories.name: Product diversification
ideas: Manufacture related garments (e.g., hijabs, modest fashion accessories)
Create differentiated product lines for different occasions (casual, formal, festive)

recommendation: Go. The client should purchase the new machine.

The cumulative 5-year contribution of $1,875K significantly exceeds the $1M machine cost, yielding a net profit of $875K and a break-even in approximately 3.5 years — well within the 5-year payback criterion.
All competitors are at maximum capacity, so the client is uniquely positioned to capture 100% of incremental market growth from the expanding target demographic.
risks: Competitor expansion: if even one competitor adds capacity and captures half the incremental demand, the 5-year contribution splits to roughly $937.5K, resulting in a loss of approximately $62.5K
Demand risk: if demand for Abayas declines (e.g., cultural shifts, regulation changes), incremental volume projections may not materialize
Capacity utilization: after 5 years, the client will only use about 62.5% of the extra capacity, meaning significant idle capacity remains
next_steps: Explore strategies to utilize idle capacity: expand locally (new age groups, new designs, price competitiveness) or pursue export markets in other GCC countries
Monitor competitor capacity decisions closely and consider pre-emptive market share moves
Evaluate opportunities for product diversification using the new machine capacity
